facts.text: Simple is a differentiable physics engine that uses Pinocchio for dynamics computations and Coal for collision detection
The upstream README states the code is released under the permissive BSD-3 license
The simple Python package re-exports the compiled simple_pywrap extension
exposeSimulator exposes the C++ Simulator class through SimulatorPythonVisitor
The sandbox imports mujoco in a try block and sets mujoco_imported false when the optional dependency is missing
runMujocoXML prints 'Can't run, need to install mujoco' when the optional mujoco import failed
The humanoid sandbox script sets its model path to ./sandbox/robots/humanoid.xml
Without --mujoco the script builds a Pinocchio model and geometry from the MJCF
The Simple-engine loop calls sim.reset() and sim.step(q, v, zero_torque, dt)
With --mujoco the script calls runMujocoXML on the same model path
SimulationArgs.dt defaults to 1e-3 s
runMujocoXML loads an .xml model with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path, creates MjData and calls mujoco.mj_step
runMujocoXML sets the loaded model's opt.timestep to args.dt
The served model file carries a DeepMind Technologies Limited copyright notice and the Apache License, Version 2.0
The served model file is the MuJoCo Humanoid model
The model's option element sets a 0.005 s timestep
The top-level default motor element sets ctrlrange -1 1 with ctrllimited true
The torso body starts at 0 0 1.282 and carries a freejoint named root
The model has 21 hinge joints: three abdomen, six per leg (hip x/z/y, knee, ankle y/x) and three per arm (shoulder1, shoulder2, elbow)
The worldbody has a floor box with size 10 10 0.1 at position 0 0 -0.1
The contact section excludes waist_lower against thigh_right and thigh_left
Two fixed tendons named hamstring_right and hamstring_left couple hip_y and knee with coefficients .5 and -.5 and a range of -0.3 to 2
The model has 21 motor actuators, one per hinge joint, each with an explicit gear
The model defines four keyframes: squat, stand_on_left_leg, prone and supine

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the model for one free joint and 21 hinge joints, 21 motor actuators, the inherited ctrlrange and the 0.005 s option step, then moves each directly actuated joint with a placeholder first-order motor model; it computes no inertia, torque, contact, friction, tendon, joint-limit or actuator dynamics and produces no MuJoCo trajectory

the stand-in does not integrate the free base, resolve the floor contact, apply the two hamstring tendons, the contact exclusions, the joint ranges, damping, stiffness, armature or gear forces; the humanoid cannot stand or fall on the fake
the fake reset starts the free joint at a placeholder pose (zeros plus an identity quaternion) and every hinge at zero; the real model's qpos0 and its four keyframes are not reproduced
the fake does not implement mj_getState/mj_setState/mj_stateSize, so a snapshot on the fake uses the bridge's basic time/qpos/qvel/act/ctrl profile, not MuJoCo's full integration state
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran (no network, no pip), so the stand-in was not compared with the real engine
